name: room
text: Room opened — goal: Deliver: Push link coverage toward 100% at +5%/day (the access gate)

name: Reel
text: Adopt the **5-second gate + 10% semantic confidence score** as the unified content gate. It’s the fastest way to hit 100% link coverage without drowning in false positives—longer gates waste time, shorter ones let junk through. The trade-off is missing some valid links, but the 10% buffer keeps misses rare while still moving us +5%/day.

name: Scriv
text: The 5-second gate + 10% semantic score risks letting through clips that are coherent but irrelevant—like a 5-second clip of a tree swaying in the wind that scores 10% on "nature" but adds zero value. A better alternative is a **10-second gate + 20% semantic confidence**, paired with a manual review of the top 10% of low-confidence clips to catch false positives. Settle it with a side-by-side test: run both gates on the same 1000-clip sample and measure precision vs. recall—if the 10/20 gate loses fewer valid links without a flood of junk, adopt it.

name: Chisel
text:
Adopt the **5-second gate + 30% semantic relevance threshold**. This keeps the gate fast while filtering out most noise—longer gates slow the pipeline, and lower thresholds let irrelevant clips slip through. The trade-off is missing some valid links, but the 30% buffer balances speed and quality better than the 10% or 20% options.

name: Sift
text: Chisel’s 30% semantic threshold is a gamble on false negatives: it will reject clips that are short but meaningful—like a 6-second clip of a rare animal behavior that scores 28% on "wildlife." The real risk is crippling the access gate by starving it of valid links, not noise. Settle it with a live A/B: run 5s/10% vs. 5s/30% on the same day’s batch and measure how many *missed* links each gate blocks—then pick the one that loses fewer.

name: Scope
text: Adopt the **5-second gate + 20% semantic relevance threshold** with a **10% manual review reserve** for edge cases. This balances speed and accuracy—longer gates slow the pipeline, lower thresholds let noise through, and the reserve catches missed valid links without drowning in false positives. The trade-off is accepting a small increase in manual review work to protect the access gate’s momentum.

name: Scriv
text: Scope’s 5-second gate + 20% threshold with a 10% manual reserve still risks crippling the access gate by over-filtering valid links—like rejecting a 5.5-second clip of a rare animal that scores 19% on "wildlife" but is the only usable shot in a 10-hour reel. Settle it with a live A/B test: run the 5s/20% gate against the 10s/15% gate on 5k clips, measure false negatives (missed valid links) and false positives (junk that slips through), and pick the one that hits 95%+ precision without starving the pipeline.
